questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Some of the most important factors in choosing my location for exchange were that it should be affordable and place where I could learn a new culture. As I already visited Seoul 2 years ago for 2 weeks, I had feeling of the place and I really loved what I saw and experienced. There seemed to be an amazing and social environment for exchange students as well.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: My exchange to Seoul turned out to be the best exchange I have ever been on, despite corona restrictions, I met so many wondeful people and Seoul truly has so much to offer. The city has endless oportunities and concepts to explore, there would always be something to do or see, and it is affordable to have a really nice lifestyle there as a student.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Sungkyunkwan university was very helpful and informative upon arrival, which specifically was nice do to the corona situations and rules. We had a contact person we could contact from a exchange group which made it feel like that you always had somewhere to go for questions, even if it could sometimes be a little hard to get a direct answer. But overall it was very good.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: we got a welcome package with all the information of how to apply for courses and who to contact for questions and so on. It even had some little imporant fact regarding accomodation, transportation and culture, which was super nice.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Overall information was available and good, however the language barriers could sometimes make things a little bit tricky, but google translate or the app Papago is a lifesaver to help translating documents.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was very easy to find accomodation in Seoul, airbnb and guesthouses are cheap and sometimes a little small but nice and livable.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I definetly reccomend living off campus, and to live in some of the cheaper and cooler areas like: Hongdae, sinchon or Itawon. Alot of the campus dorms have tight rules and it is just nicer to have the freedom to decide what time you want to come home and so on.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I lived in an airbnb and a guesthouse during my stay, and I was very satisfyed with both.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: As mentioned earlier the university was very good at informing but sometimes things would be in Korean on the website and if you at that time did'nt know the good translation apps it could be a little hard.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration process was good but a little complicated. For me it was online registration and you have to know what courses you want to apply for in advance, because you only have limited time to apply and remember to check that the courses you apply for are in English, especially if you are on the masters, as courses in english on the master degrees can be quite limited.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: We had a contact person we could contact through the app Kakaotalk, which is kind of a Korean version of messenger.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the 3 courses that I wanted, but I was also ready at my computer at the very moment the course registraion opened.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be ready at the time the online registration opens and remember to check what language the courses are taught in.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was very satisfyed, even though it was all online, most lectures were pre-recorded do to covid, but it worked very well. The professors English could sometimes be a bit hard to understand, but besides that I found the courses easier, but I think it depends on the courses you choose.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: For me the courses were good and easier than the ones I use to take in Denmark, however I also did alot of Korean culture courses and I knew some people who studied courses in business and mathematics who had a harder time.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching was high level and there is alot respect for the profesors. It was alot of powerpoints which was helpful if the English sometimes could be a bit hard to understand. But overall the teaching style was very good and similar to the one I use to have at UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Understanding Asien Culture, Contemporary Korean Culture and Society and Politics and Economy in Korea,

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I recommend taking the cultural courses as they are very well suited for exchange students, especially if you are on your masters.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: There wasen't any specific unexpected costs, and if there were it would be little random things which were still affordable. Make sure you always have cash on you as it isn't all places that takes foreign credit cards, also they still use cash alot many places.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food and drinks are super cheap also acommodation if you choose the right areas. Clothes and transportation are also very affordable and cheap.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The University had alot to offer, but due to covid most things at the univeristy were cancelled, however there was still so much to do outside the university.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The university had alot of clubs and opportunities for exchange students to join, more specifically sports.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: As I did'nt get to join any clubs do to covid, I reccomend people to explore Seoul and the activities the city has to offer.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: We were a group of friends that went down the southern part of South Korea called Busan. It was amazing, a place with beaches and culture to explore as well. Busan was a wondeful little getaway. We also went to Jeju Island which had the most beautiful nature and hikes. I reccomend going there when the weather is hot, people also did surfing at Jeju. Also the nature in South Korea is extremely beautiful, and I reccomend going on hikes in the mountains Buraksan and Gwanaksan. Also the national park Seoraksan was one of the most amazing places I have ever been, I reccomend going there mid/end october as the colors and leaves in the fall are stunning.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: The culture is very different and very respectful. Not many speak english but people are still very helpful and sweet. I mostly spend time with other exchange students or a few Korean friends that spoke english.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Move to the places with a lot of other exchange students. I lived in the Hongdae and Sinchon area where we were alot of students. We had our own little community, as we couldnt meet people at the campus due to covid, people would meet at bars alot, hostels or social media. I recommend being openminded and sign up for as many things as possible, especially in the beginning. I got some of the best friends for life there which I didn't expect, so be brave and open.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: the language barrier was the toughest, get some good translation apps it will make your life so much easier.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: All of it, the food and the vibe

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be open and respectful,  download the apps: Papago and google translate, also they don't have google maps in Korea so use the app: Naver map or Kakao map. Also explore as much as you can!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
If you have to do quarantine in Seoul due to covid, book an airbnb (if possible with a balcony) and make sure that they allow quarintining, the government quarantine is more expensive. If you do the quarantining in your own airbnb make sure to get a SIM card before your arrival so you can order food online, you have to have a Korean sim card to use their delivery services. You can get the Sim card send to your address in Denmark through the website:
Tracy.com
(it takes around 5 days to recieve it). Also remember a thermometer in case they still have the app symptom tracking system. Most importaintly make sure to stay in the areas that has the food delivery services, I had no problems doing quarintine in Hongdae, but I had some friends that had issues getting food delivered in other areas, And just don't get covid before departure.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The Amazing friends I made, the people were just wondeful. Also that Seoul has so much to see and offer, even though I stayed 5 months there was still alot to explore and im definetly coming back one day. As long as you are openminded and willing to explore it will be so rewarding. Check out the hikes in Seoul, the cafés and resturants. Also the little trips you can go on outside Seoul.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The language and covid rules. And of course having to go home again....

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Go to Seoul if you want to have that Asien culture experience with a little hint of Western vibes. Seoul is super modern and traditional at the same time. If you are a food lover this is the place for you, also the culture, K-pop and fashion is amazing. For me my time in Seoul was the perfect little dream world with wondeful people and so much to explore.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
